authoredPrompt: This figure contains two 2D vectors emanating from a common origin, illustrating the geometric definition of endpoint error in optical flow evaluation. The vector labeled (u, v) represents the ground truth flow vector, while the vector labeled (u-hat, v-hat) represents the predicted flow vector; both share the same base point but point in slightly different directions and have different magnitudes. A red line segment connects the tips (endpoints) of the two vectors, and this segment is labeled Endpoint error, making explicit that the loss is the Euclidean distance between the endpoint of the prediction and the endpoint of the ground truth. This figure establishes endpoint error as a vector-space distance metric, clarifying why it is sensitive to both directional and magnitude errors in the predicted flow field.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly
- Toggle between endpoint error (straight-line distance between vector tips) and angular error (angle between the two vectors) metrics, highlighting which geometric quantity each measures in the diagram
authoredContext: In supervised optical flow estimation, the most common loss is the **endpoint error**, which is the average, over the whole image, if the distance between the estimated optical flow vector, $(\hat{u},\hat{v})$ and the ground-truth vector, $(u,v)$: $$\mathcal{L} \left( \hat{\mathbf{u}}, \hat{\mathbf{v}}, \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \right) = \sum_{n,m} (\hat{u}[n,m] - u[n,m])^2 + (\hat{v}[n,m] - v[n,m])^2$$ The sum is over all the pixels in the image. Each pixel has an estimated optical flow $(\hat{u}[n,m],\hat{v}[n,m])$.

discrepancies: The predicted-vector label renders as (û, v´) — the circumflex hat on v is drawn as a prime/accent instead of a proper hat, so it does not match the source's (û,v̂)
A faint orange θ arc and θ glyph are visible at the origin in the default Endpoint-error state (gAngle at opacity 0.18), an element absent from the clean source figure
Small circular drag handles sit on both arrow tips, adding chrome not present in the source (acceptable as interaction affordance but visually extra)
Overall composition is rotated/scaled into a wider canvas with a right-hand control panel, so the at-a-glance layout differs from the source's tight two-vector crop
evaluation.notes: The two-vector-plus-red-endpoint-error topology, arrowheads, and (u,v)/Endpoint-error labels faithfully reproduce the source, and the drag/metric-toggle/demo interactions are genuinely functional and pedagogically strong; the main flaws are the mis-rendered hat on v̂ and a stray faint θ arc polluting the default Endpoint view.
action_items: Fix the (û,v̂) label so both letters carry a true circumflex hat (e.g. use SVG <tspan> with a drawn ^ or the correct combining character U+0302); currently v shows a prime-like accent.
In the default 'endpoint' metric state set gAngle opacity to 0 (not 0.18) so no faint θ arc/glyph appears, matching the clean source figure; reveal the arc only when Angular error is selected.
Consider hiding or shrinking the tip drag-handle rings in the static default state so the step-0 view reads as a drop-in replacement for the source image.
